newsitem.title: USA: Int'l standards for oranges to be developed - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Int'l standards for oranges to be developed - USDA.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Tuesday asked the U.S. produce industry to help develop international quality standards for fresh oranges, grapefuit and other fruits.

The Codex Alimentarius Commission will meet in Mexico City in September to work on quality standards for oranges, grapefruit, limes, Mexican limes, pineapples and a half-dozen other fruits and vegetables.

The USDA will review proposed Codex standards with input from the U.S. fruit and vegetable industry "to ensure that U.S. exports do not face trade barriers based on quality standards," said Lon Hatamiya, administrator of the Agricultural Marketing Service.
The Codex committee was formed in 1985 and meets every 18 months to develop standards for various fruits and vegetables.
